request.prompt:
You are clustering code review findings from the same PR. For each PAIR below, decide whether the two findings describe the SAME underlying issue — same root cause in the same code location. Different wording is fine. A finding about a DIFFERENT defect in the same file or function is NOT the same issue. Severity or aspect differences of the same root cause ARE the same issue.


For THIS scoring pass, duplicate equivalence is stricter than sharing a root cause.
You must compare the COMPLETE MATERIAL CLAIMS, including mechanism, triggering
conditions, execution path, and consequence. The same line or broad concern does
not establish equivalence. A report of wrong-category selection, a case/rename
mismatch, a crash, and a silent fallback are different claims even at one lookup.
An inactive/unbound API concern and an alleged active user-facing failure differ.
A compound report with an additional material claim does NOT equal its subset.
Differences only in wording, severity, or hedging do not create separate claims.
If the claimed mechanisms, triggers or consequences conflict, or one report adds
an unsupported/different material factual claim, return same=false. You are NOT
verifying which claim is true; do not repair or reinterpret either report to make
them match. If unsure whether their full claims are equivalent, return false.

For every numbered pair, extract what A and B actually CLAIM into mechanism,
trigger and consequence. Then list material_differences and give your equivalence
verdict, confidence and reason. same=true requires no material differences.
Return ONLY this JSON object, with EVERY pair index exactly once:
{"pairs":[{"pair":1,"a":{"mechanism":"...","trigger":"...","consequence":"..."},"b":{"mechanism":"...","trigger":"...","consequence":"..."},"material_differences":[],"same":true,"confidence":0.9,"reason":"..."}]}

PAIR 6:
A: Email-send failures are caught and reduced to console.log('Error sending AddGuestsEmails') while the mutation returns { message: 'Guests added' }. When sendAddGuestsEmails fails (SMTP outage, renderEmail throw, unbounded replyTo rejection), the organizer and all attendees receive no notification and no updated ICS, yet the user sees the 'Guests added' success toast — the failure is completely invisible to the user and unobservable beyond a server console line with no error object logged.
B: The try/catch around sendAddGuestsEmails swallows every email failure and discards the caught err entirely (console.log prints the static string 'Error sending AddGuestsEmails' without it), after which the handler returns {message: 'Guests added'} as success. When the mail provider or a template render fails during add-guests, the organizer sees the 'Guests added' success toast while no guest is ever notified, the error object is lost so operations cannot diagnose the outage, and the mutation's success return is structurally decoupled from the email side effect — a handler test running against a throwing email mock passes green, so no test can ever detect email-delivery regressions through this endpoint.

PAIR 7:
A: The check-then-createMany pattern is a TOCTOU race: concurrent requests can both pass the filter, yielding duplicate rows if there is no unique constraint on (bookingId, email) or an unhandled raw Prisma P2002 500 if there is
B: TOCTOU between the dedup read and the write: authorization and duplicate filtering happen on the findFirst snapshot with several awaits before createMany commits, so two concurrent requests adding the same guest both pass the filter and both write — producing duplicate attendees or a raw unique-constraint 500; read+write should be wrapped in a transaction or P2002 caught with a clean error

PAIR 8:
A: Error toast fallback 'unable_to_add_guests' is unreachable and raw server messages/codes are shown to users
B: Error toast fallback is dead code: the message template is always truthy so the || t('unable_to_add_guests') fallback never fires, and t() on a non-translation-key renders the raw key string
